question: Is there a concrete firmware-vs-training pipeline mismatch that could explain MLP/CNN disagreement on the real wrist?
verdict_explanation: No axis-order, sign, unit, gravity-recursion, normalisation-constant or window-layout mismatch between firmware and training was found. Channel order/layout/features are parity-verified (HIL 0 flips), units are m/s^2 and rad/s on both sides (library source + HIFD gyro/quaternion rate ratio ~1.00), headers equal the pickled models, and the device at rest gives p~0.001 for both models while a strong fall gave 1.00/1.00. The remaining unverifiable assumptions (HIFD sensor frame vs Bio-Band mounting, quaternion convention) do not reproduce the observed pattern on their own: re-running the real firmware chain on HIFD falls with 90/180 deg rotations, permutations and mirrors keeps the ensemble at 11-15/15 and rarely makes one model confident while the other is blind (per-fall peak disagreement rate, mean 0.0571 and worst single transform 0.2), whereas the device shows 3/6 episodes with such disagreement (Fisher p~4e-4 vs HIFD 1/104; binomial P(>=3/6) = 0.0033 at the mean rotation rate and 0.0989 at the worst), so a wrist-mounting-angle difference is a possible contributor but not a sufficient explanation by itself. Amplitude/bandwidth shifts typical of a soft mattress fall and a different wearer make the MLP and CNN disagree in both directions, which matches the wrist logs. Evidence is indirect: no raw wrist IMU samples were saved, so the true Bio-Band input distribution is not compared directly; the sample is 6 events from one wearer.

findings.item: Gravity handling (which axis is gravity when worn)
findings.firmware: raw accel incl. gravity -> first-order low-pass gravity estimate alpha 0.98 initialised with the first sample -> lin = a - g_est (g_est updated BEFORE subtraction, so it includes the current sample) (ai_model.cpp:294-311)
findings.training: HIFD lin + gravity rebuilt from the quaternion (ASSUMED gravity = R^T [0,0,g], i.e. body->world quaternion), then 21 Hz low-pass, +-16 g clip, identical alpha 0.98 recursion with grav[0]=a[0] (preproc.py)
findings.evidence: Recursion and initialisation are identical. Static gravity direction is removed by the high-pass, so only dynamic orientation changes matter. Training-side assumptions tested: opposite quaternion convention -> ens 13/15 (identity 14), 'lin is world-frame' -> 14/15, no meaningful disagreement increase. Under the assumed convention the HIFD wrist gravity direction in the sensor frame is spread widely (mean [0.0954, -0.3306, 0.3625], std [0.5164, 0.4246, 0.5507], dominant axis x/y/z fractions [0.2896, 0.2527, 0.4577]): there is no single 'gravity axis' that the models can rely on. The Bio-Band resting gravity direction could not be checked (no raw rest samples saved).

findings.item: Mounting orientation of the band vs HIFD wrist sensor
findings.firmware: MPU6050 fixed on the board, axes = board axes; the strap does not fix the angle on the wrist (BAO_CAO sec. 12 item 4: case/strap to fix the MPU6050 orientation is future work)
findings.training: HIFD: left wrist, unknown axis mapping; augmentation only random rotations up to +-30 deg (fw_aug0-2, rot='small', bias 0.15); the deployed models were NOT trained with SO(3) rotations; 36/42 MLP features are axis-dependent (BAO_CAO sec. 11)
findings.evidence: Applying 90/180 deg rotations, axis permutations and a mirror to subjects 19-21 and re-running the real firmware chain: ensemble detects 11-15/15 (identity 14/15); per-fall MLP/CNN peak disagreement rate mean 0.0571, worst 0.2; window-level |mlp-cnn|>0.5 on fall windows rises from 0.016 to 0.1499 (mean) / 0.3279 (max). Binomial P(>=3 of 6 episodes disagree) = 0.0033 at the mean rotation rate, 0.0989 at the worst. Orientation raises disagreement a lot at window level but rarely enough to make one model sure and the other blind on a fall; it cannot be excluded as a contributor, but it is unlikely to be the only cause. CNN is the more orientation-sensitive model on ADL windows (rot z -90: 3.4% of ADL windows >= 0.9 vs 0% for the MLP).
